class_guess: Skelet 1-like: binary counter whose digits are field parities, with re-pairing bounces
summary: Binary counter on budget fields (10)^f 1; parities are the digits; dead fields re-pair; no halt to 2.37e14.
mechanism: At every D:R event the tape is a list of fields [f]=(10)^f 1 joined by separators | (00), + (11) or # (000); the last field L is the growing end.

Each half-cycle the head walks left over even fields to the first odd field (or a + or #), takes 1 from the field just left of it and adds 3 to L: the field parities are the digits of a binary counter (ruler sequence).

A field that reaches 0 becomes a # separator; the next carry into it is a uniform re-pairing bounce (+2 to the field right of it, +1 to the rest, all separators +, new L = 1). A carry past the far end is the same bounce for the whole tape. Exact simulator: no halt to 2.367e14; the 4 starts share every event and differ only in the first field.

rules.name: ODD
rules.from: .. f_d | f_j(odd) | e .. | L  (all fields right of f_j even)
rules.cases: f_d >= 1 (1 -> 0 included); separator left of f_d is | or +

rules.name: ODD-across-plus
rules.cases: d >= 2 (d = 1 at the far end: 1 + j -> 0 | j-1)

strategy: Prove a token-level invariant INV (allowed local patterns, budgets of the fields next to # and +, far-end prefix set) closed under the 9 validated rules plus the far-end table; nonhalting follows. One argument for the table; 179/265/597 are #24-style deltas (own base segment into the same family, first field as a parameter).
risks: The global invariant is open: 255 of 4,000 random tiny token lists halt, so INV must exclude bad local patterns for all field values.
Far-end prefix set looks small (about 10 shapes in 35 x 12 hand-built deaths) but is not shown closed; line 75's natural far-end death is due just after 2.4e14.
The case table (9 rules plus far-end variants) is larger than #3's; the formal stage may exceed 1 agent-day.

checkpoint_questions.text: Counter figure: in every row exactly one non-green column is red, and each column switches grey/white only in its red rows (so field parity = counter digit)?
Death figure: the 0-field's gap widens into one wider gap, the field left of it shrinks once, and then one long V re-groups every field to its right and starts a new short field at the right end?

Before proof.md on #3's route, should we spend 2 h on an abstract closure search (fields as {0,1,2,>=3} x parity, separators | + #, far-end prefixes)? If it closes, it is the invariant and a regular-certificate attempt for all 4 lines.
